items.title: James "Sing" Miller Interview, 1964-12-11
items.q: Well, I'll tell you who had the band was Old Man Robichaux.

ctx.x: Can you remember some of the other bands you've worked with? You told about that first band that you played, the one on Dryad Street. I worked with Paul Barber, I worked with George Lewis, I worked with George Williams, I worked with the average band around here. Yeah, I guess you worked with a whole bunch of them. Yeah, around here. Like most of the musicians. I worked with Kit Howard, Sheik, Thomas, you know I work with Thomas now. I work with Thomas now. But I worked with Peter Burkhardt, I worked with Willie…

12-inch records, big, big records, those large records. The big horn and all, some of them. The horn sticking out on the victuals and all of them. In other words, some of them would stand the victual and wind the victuals, every day they had no piano. Yeah. And a lot of times, guys like I said would come in with the harmonica and guitars and things. They might come in with maybe a G-hop or E-flat harmonica. And if you were any kind of piano player at all, you knew just what he did from the hop that you could tune…

About six or seven in the band you say? About six or seven in the band. About time, yeah. In other words, the band had a coffee in the show. Besides, you know, the performers and packing all the different medicine up and bringing around. Yeah. Yeah, about five, I know. I think about five, yeah. Was the medicine any good or was it just a racket? Some people say it was just soup. That's what I wonder. I've heard you. Some people say it was just soup. Or colored water and things like that sometimes. I think they…
